prompt: Marketing doubled sign-ups, but most new users left within a week.
tells: most new users left within a week
why: More sign-ups into a leaky bucket don't help. Fix retention.
trap: Sign-ups aren't vanity here; the problem is people leaving.

prompt: The retention curve drops to zero instead of flattening, so the team pauses growth spending.
tells: drops to zero instead of flattening
why: A curve that never flattens means no lasting value yet.
trap: It's not a test; it's the shape of retention.

prompt: Improving the first-week experience raised month-3 retention more than any ad campaign.
trap: It was impactful, but the lesson is retention.

prompt: Before buying more ads, the team calls users who cancelled.
trap: It's talking to users, but in service of retention.

prompt: Each customer costs $80 to acquire but leaves before paying $50.
why: If customers don't stay, growth loses money.
trap: It's not vanity; it's unit economics of retention.

prompt: The team focuses on getting users to come back on day two.
trap: It's not the north star; it's retention.
